note: Three checks of the revised estimate script, its recorded output and the accompanying documentation, made by AI agents on 2026-11-20 against the commit that first added them. 'numbers' recomputed every figure from the records; 'code' read and exercised analysis/pilot_estimate.py and scripts/prune_setup_files.sh; 'stranger' read as a third party with only the repository. Each finding names the text as it stood in that commit; all were acted on in the commit that added this file, so the quoted text may no longer be present. None changed a figure of the estimate. They are a check on consistency with the recorded data, not evidence about the proof.

result.checked: I read the HEAD commit's diff for every listed document and recomputed its numbers from the sources, using python3 -I and writing nothing to the repo. Sources: pilot_estimate.json, phases.tsv, disk.txt, setup.tsv, import_only.tsv, import_probe.tsv and status.json in both run directories, the gzipped modules.tsv and check_results.txt, ledger.tsv, gcp_family_rates.json, pilot_targets.json, mapped-files-sample.txt, pilot_estimate_review.json, and the import graph (an 8,000-module closure sample, and a count of names that are a dotted prefix of another). These all matched: the machine prices from per-vCPU and per-GiB rates (1.7789, 1.3552, 1.0136, 0.7721), the disk price per hour (0.083 and 0.259), all 15 cells of the cost table (hours times rates plus 6 hours of disk), the hour cases (442, 434, 469 and 453 CPU-hours; 15.6, 14.0, 17.9 and 15.4 hours), and the cross-check (175,187/3.32 = 14.7 h; ×1.06 = 15.5; checker 14.1). The ledger (0.57 and 5.82 USD; 17 min; 2 h 55 min), the 29,633 and 1,439 olean counts, the 2,233 and 565 zero-status checks, the setup time (76 s), the contention (1.66) and the slope (0.226) all matched. So did the 16-to-32-job changes (+7% and +52%), median CPU 5.88, the longest wall time 409 s, the memory figures (504/765/8,130 MB) and disk per module (0.72/5.53 MB). The mapped-file arithmetic (52,260; about 236,000; about 12,600 headroom), share of closures above 17,860 (3.4%) and above 12,000 (5.0%), the 114 prefixes, kern.maxvnodes 263,168 on this 24 GB Mac, and the reviewers' cited figures (26.7/29.7/36.4, 58/64/79, 4.7%, 327 and 92, 0.8 h, 27 and 13) all matched too. The problems below are the ones confirmed.

findings.where: Section 8.2, step 1: "A plain regression of CPU on closure size gives a slope of 0.048 seconds per 1,000 imports with a standard error of 0.049"
findings.problem: The slope is wrong. pilot_estimate.json gives compile_model.plain_regression.per_1000_imports = 0.046, and the low case uses slope 4.6e-05. The standard error 0.049 is right.
findings.correction: Change 0.048 to 0.046.
findings.confirmed_how: Read records/cloud/pilot/pilot_estimate.json (plain_regression and cases.low.slope).

findings.where: Section 2: "The private share was not measured separately."; Section 6 table: "With a penalty for deeper modules of 1.1 to 2.0 times ... No measurement supports either end" and "Kernel replay of every module afterwards | Not known..."; Section 6 text: "that start-up time is likely to grow as the number of finished modules grows"
findings.problem: The new intro says that wherever section 9 answers a question an earlier section leaves open, "the earlier section says so". Sections 5 and 7 were given such pointers, but sections 2 and 6 were not, although section 9's table answers them by name ("sections 2 and 7", "section 6" three times). So these older passages now contradict section 9 without saying so. Section 9 gives private memory as median 0.5 GB plus 13 KB per import, the depth penalty as about 6 percent, the replay as 8.3 CPU-s per module and about 14 h, and restart as 4 to 9 s with up to 30,000 built.
findings.correction: Add a one-line pointer in each place. In section 2: "Measured later on Linux: median 0.5 GB per process, see section 9". In section 6: "Measured later on Linux: deeper modules cost about 6 percent more on average; replay 8.3 CPU-s per module, about 14 hours on 32 vCPUs; restart 4 to 9 s with up to 30,000 built; see section 9".
findings.confirmed_how: Read the HEAD versions of docs/performance-notes.md sections 2, 6 and 9, and compared them with pilot_estimate.json.

findings.where: "In progress: about 22,000 of 175,187 modules on a Mac, zero failures so far"; also docs/performance-notes.md section 4: "Run without `--delete` on the real build at 23,057 setup files, it found 149.9 GB, of which 148.3 GB belonged to finished modules"
findings.problem: No committed record backs these numbers. records/mac-build/build-status.txt holds only start and end lines. The only dated count elsewhere is 11,162 (docs/verification-criteria.md), and CLAIMS K4 sends readers to records/ for the dated counts. A git grep of HEAD finds 22,000, 23,057, 149.9 and 148.3 nowhere under records/. This breaks the rule that every claim is tied to evidence a stranger can check.
findings.correction: Add a dated record under records/mac-build/ (for example the output of scripts/06_progress.sh and of scripts/prune_setup_files.sh in report mode, with a timestamp), and cite it from both places. Otherwise give the figure with its time and mark it as unrecorded.
findings.confirmed_how: Ran git grep over HEAD for the figures and read records/mac-build/build-status.txt.

findings.where: Section 5: "The pilot measured it: about 16 hours for the build and 14 for the kernel replay (section 8)."
findings.problem: The pilot did not measure 16 and 14 hours. They are an extrapolation: section 8.2 calls them an estimate, and CLAIMS M6 says "Extrapolated from M4". Saying "measured" overstates the evidence behind the numbers.
findings.correction: "From the pilot's measurements it is estimated at about 16 hours for the build and 14 for the kernel replay (section 8)."
findings.confirmed_how: Compared the sentence with section 8.2, CLAIMS.md M6 and the hours in pilot_estimate.json, which are computed rather than observed.

findings.where: Section 8.2: "The whole tree's compiled output is about 127 GB, Mathlib's adds about 7 GB"
findings.problem: The same quantity has a different value elsewhere. docs/performance-notes.md sections 2, 4 and 5 say Mathlib's own compiled files are 5.9 GB. No source gives 7 GB. The nearest figure is the 6.6 GB file-backed base per process in section 8.1, which also includes Lean's library and so is a different quantity.
findings.correction: Use one figure: "Mathlib's adds about 6 GB (5.9 GB)", or say the 7 GB is Mathlib plus Lean's own library and cite where it comes from.
findings.confirmed_how: Searched both documents for the Mathlib size and read pilot_estimate.json memory.file_backed_mb.base = 6598.

findings.where: Section 8.1: "6.6 GB plus 0.57 MB per imported project module, which projects to about 104 GB for the last module" (also 8.2 "the last modules each touch about 104 GB")
findings.problem: The units are mixed. In the stated units, 6,598 MB + 0.572 MB × 175,186 = 106,804 MB, which is about 107 GB. The 104 comes from dividing by 1,024 (GiB), while 6.6 GB comes from dividing by 1,000. That is a gap of about 3 percent, more than rounding.
findings.correction: Either "6.4 GiB plus 0.57 MiB per module ... about 104 GiB", or "6.6 GB plus 0.57 MB ... about 107 GB", and the same in section 8.2.
findings.confirmed_how: Recomputed from pilot_estimate.json memory.file_backed_mb (base 6598, per_import 0.572, projected 104).

findings.where: "Lake writes about 1.5 TB for the whole tree, nine tenths of it regenerable setup files"; also docs/performance-notes.md section 1 "or about 200 GB if the JSON is removed as modules finish" (cites section 4)
findings.problem: The disk total for the whole tree has three different values: about 1.5 TB here, about 1.4 TB in performance-notes sections 1 and 4 (with 1.5 TB as the allowance), and 1.1 to 1.3 TB in cloud-notes section 9 and pilot_estimate.json (1.07 + 0.127 TB). The total without setup files is "about 150 GB" in performance-notes section 4 and cloud-notes section 9 (peak 152 GB in the JSON). The performance-notes summary says "about 200 GB" and cites section 4, which does not contain 200.
findings.correction: Replication guide: "Lake writes about 1.2 to 1.4 TB for the whole tree; allow 1.5 TB". Performance-notes summary: "about 150 GB (allow 200 GB) if the JSON is removed as modules finish".
findings.confirmed_how: Compared the passages and pilot_estimate.json disk (setup_files_tb_full_tree 1.07, compiled_tb_full_tree 0.127, peak 152).

findings.where: Sections 2 and 5 (older text): "memory-mapping the compiled files of Mathlib and the libraries beneath it: 8,690 modules" and "A module that imports only Mathlib loads 8,690 files"
findings.problem: This now contradicts the new mapped-files-sample.txt and the new section 7, which count 10,452 library modules (8,651 Mathlib and its packages plus 1,801 of Lean's own library). Cloud-notes point 8 rests on exactly this difference: the 1,801 are said to come on top of Mathlib's count.
findings.correction: Change it to "10,452 library modules (8,651 from Mathlib and its packages, 1,801 from Lean's own library; records/mac-build/mapped-files-sample.txt)", or say what the 8,690 counts (setup-file entries) and that Lean's library adds 1,801.
findings.confirmed_how: Read records/mac-build/mapped-files-sample.txt (10,452 = 8,651 + 1,801) against performance-notes sections 2, 5 and 7.

findings.where: Section 8.1 row "CPU per module at 32 jobs | Mean 8.5 seconds, median 5.9. 106 modules took over a minute of wall time; the longest took 409 seconds"
findings.problem: The 106 counts finished compiles from every window, including the 16-, 24- and 8-job sweeps. Restricted to the 32-job windows the row names (cold, deepA, deepB, sweep2, sweep4), the count is 95. The mean 8.54 and median 5.88 do match the 32-job windows.
findings.correction: "95 modules at 32 jobs (106 across all windows) took over a minute of wall time".
findings.confirmed_how: Read pilot-20261120-162141/modules.tsv.gz with Python, dropped processes ending within 3.5 s of a window's end, and counted wall_s > 60 by phase.

findings.where: Header: "It is 5 to 6 MB for a module that imports only Mathlib"
findings.problem: performance-notes section 4 gives the measured size for a module that imports only Mathlib as 6.43 MB. 5.53 MB is the pilot's mean over all modules, not the Mathlib-only size.
findings.correction: "It is about 6.4 MB for a module that imports only Mathlib", or "5.5 to 6.5 MB on average".
findings.confirmed_how: Compared the header with performance-notes section 4 and with pilot_estimate.json disk.setup_file_mb_per_module = 5.53.

findings.where: Line 36: "Not yet possible. A random sample of 24 compiled modules was replayed and all 24 passed"
findings.problem: This older passage, not touched by the commit, now lists fewer kernel-replay samples than README.md, CLAIMS.md K3 and the pilot records, which give 24, 565 and 2,233.
findings.correction: "Not yet possible. Samples of 24 (Mac), 565 and 2,233 (cloud) compiled modules were replayed and all passed".
findings.confirmed_how: Ran git grep over HEAD and counted pilot and rehearsal check_results.txt.gz (2,233 and 565 lines, all status 0).

result.checked: Reproduction: ran analysis/pilot_estimate.py with the five --config arguments from docs/cloud-notes.md 8.2 and compared the parsed JSON with records/cloud/pilot/pilot_estimate.json. The two are identical. A run with no --config also matches everywhere except 'configurations'. A copy of the results directory with every file gunzipped gives the same output, so plain files work. Logic: read every step against the docstring and section 8.2. Killed rows are dropped only in windows that lake_log_summary.tsv does not mark exit 0. The check window is always treated as time-boxed, which is correct: the dropped checker rows end together with under 0.6 s of CPU and are absent from check_results. Unnamed '?' rows are excluded from the fits but counted in the process totals. Among finished rows no named module repeats (29,388 distinct out of 29,388 named). The proration in efficiency() is right if CPU is spread evenly over each process's life, and killed rows correctly contribute the CPU they used. I built altered copies of the pilot data in a temp dir (no deepB, no check window, deepB renamed) and ran the script on each. prune_setup_files.sh: read the code. Built a scratch Lake tree with finished, unfinished, no-.olean and too-young modules, a symlinked setup file and a symlinked directory, then ran it with /bin/bash 3.2 in report mode and with --delete on a scratch copy only. It removed only the two finished *.setup.json entries, removed the symlink but not its target, did not descend into the symlinked directory, left .c files alone, worked with no lib directory, and exited 1 on bad arguments. I checked the ordering claim against the Lake 4.33.1 source in ~/.elan (Build/Actions.lean and Build/Common.lean): the setup file is written inside the build action and the trace by buildAction afterwards, so the 'finished' test is sound. 00_check_prereqs.sh: bash -n passes. Compared the new messages with records/mac-build/mapped-files-sample.txt (52,260 base files, about 1.05 per project module, about 236,000 projected; kern.maxvnodes here is 263,168) and they agree. No bash 5 binary was available, so the script was exercised only on bash 3.2.

findings.where: line 45: CONFIGS = [c.split(':') for c in args('--config')] or [...]
findings.problem: A --config NAME that contains a colon makes the unpacking at line 240 ('for name, rate, gb in CONFIGS') fail. Confirmed: --config "a:b:1.78:440" raises 'ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3, got 4)'. The names are free text (the documented ones already contain commas), so a colon is easy to add by accident.
findings.correction: Split from the right: CONFIGS = [c.rsplit(':', 2) for c in args('--config')] or [...]. Optionally reject entries that do not give exactly three fields with a clear message.
findings.confirmed_how: Ran the script with --config "a:b:1.78:440" against the recorded pilot and got the traceback.

findings.where: line 121-122: tail = [p for p in full if p['c'] > 8000]; _, b_tail, se_tail = ols(...)
findings.problem: The script assumes at least two modules above closure 8000 were compiled at full jobs. With none, st.mean raises StatisticsError. With one, sxx is 0 and the division at line 107 raises ZeroDivisionError. With only a few, b_tail is used anyway in the high case (max(b_tail, s_phys) * 1.10) with no warning. Confirmed: removing the deepB window from phases.tsv crashes at line 122, because all the large closures came from deepB. The same unguarded ols/st.mean pattern also affects an empty 'full' list at line 120.
findings.correction: Guard the tail fit: if len(tail) < some minimum (for example 30), report it as null and use s_phys for the high case (or s_phys raised by a stated factor), and record that in the output. Give ols() a clear error, or a None return, when fewer than 2 points or sxx == 0.
findings.confirmed_how: Made a copy of the pilot directory with deepB lines removed from phases.tsv; the run failed at line 122 with 'StatisticsError: mean requires at least one data point'.

findings.where: lines 188-190: c_a, c_b, c_se = ols([p['c'] for p in chk.values()], ...); ...; eff_check = windows['check']['useful_cpu_per_thread_second']
findings.problem: A pilot with no check window, or no named checker rows, cannot be estimated at all. ols on the empty list raises StatisticsError at line 188, and windows['check'] would then raise KeyError at line 190. probe_fit('checker') also fails if import_probe.tsv has no checker rows. The kernel_share_of_cpu expression at line 265 divides by the total checker CPU, which is zero in that case.
findings.correction: If chk is empty or 'check' is not in windows, skip the checker model (or fall back to the 'alone' probe fit if that exists), leave check hours out of billed_hours or mark them unknown, and say so in the output, rather than crashing.
findings.confirmed_how: Made a copy of the pilot directory with the check lines removed from phases.tsv; the run failed at line 188 (ols -> st.mean, StatisticsError).

findings.where: line 184: eff_expected = windows['deepB'][...] if 'deepB' in windows else st.mean(... for b in full_windows); line 206: if ph not in ('cold', 'deepA', 'deepB'): continue
findings.problem: Window names are hard-coded. docs/cloud-notes.md 8.2 step 3 says utilisation is 'measured inside the longest window'. The code takes the window named deepB and otherwise falls back to the mean over all full-job windows, including the 6-minute sweeps, which is the averaging review point 3 rejected. The open-files regression silently uses only windows with those three names. Confirmed by renaming deepB to deepX in a copy of the data: the open-file regression dropped from 1,311 to 511 samples, its per-module coefficient went from 2.09 to 4.41, and the projection for the last module went from 429,033 to 837,571. Expected build hours changed from 15.6 to 15.5.
findings.correction: Choose the window from the data: longest = max(full_windows, key=lambda b: ends[b] - starts[b]) for eff_expected, and use every BUILD window with jobs == VCPUS (or every BUILD window) for the open-file regression. Alternatively, fail with a clear message when the expected names are missing.
findings.confirmed_how: Ran the script on a copy of the pilot data with 'deepB' replaced by 'deepX' in every file and compared the output with the original run.

findings.where: vn=$(sysctl -n kern.maxvnodes 2>/dev/null || echo 0) ... and mm=$(cat /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
findings.problem: When the sysctl or the /proc file cannot be read, the value falls back to 0. The script then prints 'files-in-use limit: 0' or 'memory-map limit: 0' as if 0 were the measured limit. It also prints the NOTE ('close to this limit' / 'this is too low for the full build'), which states as fact something that was not read. If either command prints something non-numeric, the [ -lt ] test also gives an 'integer expression expected' error.
findings.correction: Use an empty value for 'could not be read': vn=$(sysctl -n kern.maxvnodes 2>/dev/null) and mm=$(cat /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count 2>/dev/null). Print 'unknown (could not read kern.maxvnodes)' and skip the comparison when the value is empty or not a whole number, e.g. case "$vn" in ''|*[!0-9]*) ...;; esac.
findings.confirmed_how: Read the added lines in git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- scripts/00_check_prereqs.sh and followed the fallback by hand; bash -n passes, so this is behaviour, not syntax.

findings.where: line 227: 'A plain regression of CPU on closure size gives a slope of 0.048 seconds per 1,000 imports with a standard error of 0.049'
findings.problem: The committed script and pilot_estimate.json give compile_model.plain_regression.per_1000_imports = 0.046, not 0.048. The standard error, 0.049, matches.
findings.correction: Change 0.048 to 0.046.
findings.confirmed_how: Re-ran the documented command; the output equals the recorded pilot_estimate.json, which has per_1000_imports 0.046 and standard_error 0.049.

findings.where: lines 7-8: 'The compiler reads the file once, when it starts on that module.'
findings.problem: In Lake 4.33.1 (Build/Actions.lean, compileLeanModule), when postponeCompile is set the setup file is read a second time: leanir is run with setupFile as its first argument after lean exits. Both reads happen before buildAction writes the .trace, so the 'finished' test and the deletion stay safe. The header's 'once, when it starts' is still inaccurate.
findings.correction: Say that the setup file is read by the compiler, and by leanir when compilation is postponed, while the module is being built, and never after its .trace is written.
findings.confirmed_how: Read ~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.33.1/src/lean/lake/Lake/Build/Actions.lean lines 27-99 and Build/Common.lean buildAction (lines 307-327).

result.checked:
I read the HEAD commit's diff for README.md, CLAIMS.md, docs/cloud-notes.md (all of it, including the new sections 8 and 9), docs/performance-notes.md, docs/replication-guide.md, cloud/gcp/README.md, the records READMEs, scripts/prune_setup_files.sh, the scripts/00_check_prereqs.sh diff and analysis/pilot_estimate.py. I also read every small pilot record file and the decompressed contents of all six .gz files.

I re-ran the section 8.2 command into a temp directory with python3 -I. Its output is JSON-identical to records/cloud/pilot/pilot_estimate.json. I re-derived the main figures from the raw records: window rates, 29,633 and 1,439 .olean counts, 2,233 and 565 checker exit statuses (all 0), costs from ledger seconds, and per-module disk. I also computed the import-closure distribution from import_graph.json.gz: max 175,186 (one module), 5.1% above 12,000, 3.4% above 17,860, 27 above 50,000, 13 above 100,000. All of these match the text.

I checked every relative markdown link in the changed .md files against git ls-files, and all resolve. I checked that every flag mentioned for prune_setup_files.sh (--delete, --min-age, --project, --help) and for pilot_estimate.py (--config, --out, --vcpus) exists in the script, as do `watch`, the vm.max_map_count value in pilot_guest.sh, the 114-prefix skip in 09_kernel_replay.sh and the disk provisioning in pilot_local.sh.

`python3 -I scripts/dev/scrub.py check` printed "OK - no hits; scanned 95 file(s)", with exit 0. That scan decompresses gzip. My own regex scan of every pilot file, including the decompressed .gz contents, found no IP address, hostname, instance name, e-mail, bucket, project, billing ID, home path or user name. It found only /mnt/work, /dev/nvme0n1 and n2, the zone us-east1-b, and module names containing "Instance". The gzip headers carry no file name and mtime 0. I printed nothing from config.env or .private-patterns.

findings.where: line 104: "The pilot measured it: about 16 hours for the build and 14 for the kernel replay (section 8)." (also line 5: "Where section 8 and an earlier section disagree, section 8 is the measurement.")
findings.problem: The 16 and 14 hours are an extrapolation, not a measurement. pilot_estimate.py projects them from 29,633 modules with closures up to 17,860, and section 8.4 itself says the top of the graph is unmeasured. Line 5 also calls all of section 8 'the measurement', although 8.2 is an estimate.
findings.correction: Line 104: "The pilot's measurements, extrapolated in section 8.2, give an estimate of about 16 hours for the build and 14 for the kernel replay; nothing above 17,860 imports was measured." Line 5: "... section 8 supersedes it: 8.1 is measured, 8.2 is an estimate built on it."
findings.confirmed_how: Read the line and compared it with cloud-notes 8.2 and 8.4 and with pilot_estimate.json (hours.expected build_hours 15.6, check_hours 14.0, observed.largest_closure_compiled 17860).

findings.where: M6 paragraph: "It rests on measured import costs up to closures of 17,860 and was reviewed by three independent agents, whose criticism is recorded beside it"; also README.md: "three independent reviews of it"
findings.problem: The reviews were of the first version of the estimate (26.7, 29.7 and 36.4 hours; 58, 64 and 79 USD). The figures in M6 and in the README (31 hours, 58 USD, 53 to 74) come from the revised script, which no one reviewed. A reader would take the current numbers as review-checked. records/cloud/pilot/README.md and pilot_estimate_review.json's own note state this correctly.
findings.correction: CLAIMS: "... a first version of it was reviewed by three AI agents, whose criticism is recorded beside it; the revised figures here were not re-reviewed." README: "three AI reviews of a first version of it".
findings.confirmed_how: Read pilot_estimate_review.json 'note' ("reviews of the first version ... The script was revised afterwards") and cloud-notes 8.3 ("The first version of the script gave 26.7, 29.7 and 36.4 billed hours").

findings.where: line 20: "In progress: about 22,000 of 175,187 modules on a Mac, zero failures so far."
findings.problem: No tracked record gives a Mac count of about 22,000. The only dated count is in records/mac-build/README.md: "10,815 compiled project modules ... At 15:44". CLAIMS K4 tells the reader to see records/ for dated counts. The 22,000 figure can only be inferred indirectly from the performance-notes sentence about 23,057 setup files. This breaks the rule that each claim points to evidence.
findings.correction: Either state the recorded figure ("10,815 of 175,187 at 15:44 on 2026-11-20, per records/mac-build/"), or add a dated count to records/mac-build/ and cite it.
findings.confirmed_how: Ran git grep for 22,000, 23,057 and 10,815, and read records/mac-build/README.md line 11 and build-status.txt.

findings.where: Peak disk with setup files removed: "about 150 GB" (performance-notes section 4; cloud-notes section 9; pilot_estimate.json disk.peak_gb... 152) vs "about 200 GB" (performance-notes summary row; 00_check_prereqs.sh "roughly 200 GB"; replication-guide "200 GB to 1.5 TB"). Total written: replication-guide "Lake writes about 1.5 TB for the whole tree" vs cloud-notes section 9 "Without it the build writes 1.1 to 1.3 TB".
findings.problem: The files give two different peak figures without saying that 200 GB is 150 GB plus a margin. Section 9's "the build writes 1.1 to 1.3 TB" reads as a total, but 1.1 to 1.3 TB is the setup files alone (prune_setup_files.sh header: "1.1 to 1.3 TB ... against about 0.13 TB of compiled output"). That contradicts the 1.4 to 1.5 TB given elsewhere and leaves the reader unsure how much disk is needed.
findings.correction: Wherever 200 GB appears, write "about 150 GB projected; allow 200 GB". In cloud-notes section 9, write "Without it the setup files alone come to 1.1 to 1.3 TB, about 1.4 TB in all".
findings.confirmed_how: Read each passage, and pilot_estimate.json disk: setup_files_tb_full_tree 1.07, compiled_tb_full_tree 0.127, peak 152.

findings.where: 8.1 table, row "CPU per module at 32 jobs": "106 modules took over a minute of wall time; the longest took 409 seconds"
findings.problem: The row is scoped to 32 jobs, but modules.tsv.gz has 95 compiler rows over 60 s wall time in the 32-job phases. Across all phases it has 107 (deepA 22, deepB 64, cold 6, sweep2 3, sweep5 7, sweep6 5). pilot_estimate.py does not print the figure, so a reader cannot reproduce 106 as scoped.
findings.correction: Either "95 at 32 jobs took over a minute", or move the sentence out of the 32-job row as "Across all windows, about 106 modules took over a minute ...", and say how killed rows were treated.
findings.confirmed_how: Ran awk over gzip -dc modules.tsv.gz: kind lean, wall_s > 60, phase matching N=32 gives 95; all phases give 107; the maximum is 408.68 s.

findings.where: "bash cloud/gcp/pilot_local.sh launch rehearsal   # about 12 minutes, well under 1 USD"
findings.problem: This passage is unchanged, but this commit adds the recorded rehearsal: 17 minutes (ledger.tsv 1021 s; records/cloud/pilot/README.md "17 minutes"). The older passage now contradicts the new record.
findings.correction: "about 17 minutes, well under 1 USD (0.57 USD recorded)".
findings.confirmed_how: Compared cloud/gcp/README.md with ledger.tsv (rehearsal-20261120-160322 seconds 1021, usd 0.57) and rehearsal status.json (elapsed_s 707 for the guest).

findings.where: line 20: GCP_ZONES="us-central1-a us-central1-b us-central1-c us-central1-f"
findings.problem: The new cloud-notes section 8 says all four zones tried in us-central1 had no capacity, "which is why the zone list in `config.env` should span regions". The pilot only ran in us-east1-b. A stranger who copies the example gets exactly the zone list that failed.

findings.confirmed_how: Ran grep -n zone config.example.env and read cloud-notes section 8 first paragraph and ledger.tsv (first two rows zone 'pending', pilot us-east1-b).

findings.where: Sanitising table lists only `<WORKDIR>`, `<HOME>`, `<SCRATCH>`
